title: typeof: DuckDB's names of the types
verdict: decided: fold typeof of a column to DuckDB's name
description: DuckDB's `typeof` gives the type's SQL name in upper case: TINYINT, SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT, HUGEINT, UTINYINT, USMALLINT, UINTEGER, UBIGINT, FLOAT, DOUBLE, DECIMAL(p,s), VARCHAR, BOOLEAN, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMP_S, TIMESTAMP_MS, TIMESTAMP_NS, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, INTERVAL, BLOB, UUID; a list is its element's name and `[]` (`BIGINT[]`, `VARCHAR[][]`), a struct `STRUCT(a BIGINT, b VARCHAR)` with its field names quoted where they need it (`STRUCT("x y" INTEGER)`), a map `MAP(VARCHAR, BIGINT)`. A DECIMAL without precision is DECIMAL(18,3).
An expression's type is DuckDB's own inference: `typeof(1)` is INTEGER, `typeof(1.5)` is DECIMAL(2,1), and an INTEGER plus an INTEGER is an INTEGER. `typeof(NULL)` is `"NULL"`, quotes included.
The docs are silent on the spelling of nested types and of `"NULL"`: a docs gap.
reference: The type of a column is fixed when the plan is checked, so the Ibis producer folds `typeof(column)` to DuckDB's name as a string constant (`duckdb_type_name`, `ibis_substrait/casts.py`). Lists of these types are folded; structs and maps are refused, and so is `typeof` of an expression, whose type is the engine's inference. The plan holds DuckDB's name whichever engine runs it, so every engine gives the same string (decided by the coordinating session for #508).

evidence.observed: BIGINT, DECIMAL(18,3), TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE

evidence.sql: SELECT typeof(NULL::TIMESTAMP_MS), typeof(NULL::BIGINT[]), typeof(NULL::STRUCT("x y" INTEGER))
SELECT typeof(1), typeof(1.5), typeof('a'), typeof(NULL), typeof(1::INTEGER + 1::INTEGER)

evidence.note: typeof: the argument type's ToString(), folded at bind time
LogicalType::ToString: STRUCT(…), child + '[]' for LIST, MAP(k, v)
typeof(NULL) → "NULL"; integer, float, DECIMAL(9,3), SMALLINT[], STRUCT(n INTEGER, items VARCHAR[]) names
only typeof('abc') → VARCHAR; nested and NULL names not stated (docs gap)
